title: Crossing situation: who gives way? COLREG Rule 15 explained

scenes.label: WHO GIVES WAY?
scenes.heading: Crossing situation. Who gives way?
scenes.narration: Two power-driven vessels are crossing, and there is risk of collision. Who gives way?

scenes.label: RULE 15
scenes.heading: She is on your starboard side: you give way
scenes.narration: You are heading north. Another vessel is crossing from your starboard side, and her compass bearing is not changing. Under Rule 15, you are the give-way vessel. The usual action: alter course to starboard, early and substantially, and pass astern of her.

scenes.label: WHAT THE RULES REQUIRE
scenes.heading: Give-way and stand-on

items.title: Give-way vessel
items.text: Early and substantial action to keep well clear (Rule 16)

items.title: Avoid crossing ahead
items.text: If the circumstances of the case admit (Rule 15)

items.title: Stand-on vessel
items.text: Keeps course and speed, and keeps watching (Rule 17)

scenes.narration: The give-way vessel takes early and substantial action to keep well clear, and avoids crossing ahead of the other. The stand-on vessel keeps her course and speed, but she must keep watching.

scenes.label: KEY TAKEAWAY
scenes.heading: On your starboard side? You give way.
scenes.narration: Remember: if she is on your starboard side, you give way.
